long_biography.plain_text:
Before taking the throne, Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani moved from British schooling into military and civic responsibility. A Sandhurst graduate, he joined Qatar's armed forces, became heir apparent and chaired councils for education, health and national planning. A planned transfer of power from his father made him Amir in 2013.

That broad apprenticeship carried into a reign centred on national development and international reach. Diplomacy and mediation became prominent instruments of Qatari statecraft. Sport provided a parallel thread: as a longtime International Olympic Committee member, Tamim promoted public participation and helped develop Qatar as a global host. His continuing enthusiasm for tennis and traditional Qatari sports gives the public strategy a personal dimension.
